question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{\infty }\frac{6}{\sqrt{{z}^{5}}}\,\text{d}z & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{4}^{a}\frac{6}{\sqrt{{z}^{5}}}\,\text{d}z \\  & =6{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{4}^{a}{z}^{-5/2}\,\text{d}z \\  & =6{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-\frac{2}{3}{z}^{-3/2}]}_{4}^{a} \\  & =-4\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{\sqrt{{z}^{3}}}]}_{4}^{a} \\  & =-4\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{a}^{3}}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{{4}^{3}}}) \\  & =-4(0-\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
